device.identity_missing_policy: Record unknown explicitly; do not describe unverified physical identity as the same chip.

precision.note: The Strassen pre-add rounding is part of the algorithm under test; its numerical cost must remain visible. FP32 output differs from some historical BF16-output experiments.

timing.order: seeded balanced interleaving of arms, raw chronological records retained
timing.prepared_kernel_note: Amortized/reused-input scope; always report alongside complete call and original vs padded dimensions.
timing.repeat_bad_policy: Keep all completed samples. New complete runs may investigate drift; never replace failed/noisy rows.

preparation.padding: zero pad each needed extent to tile divisibility for custom kernels; native accepts original shape
preparation.materialization: prepared kernel uses explicitly prepared inputs, synchronizes them before timing, and records their shapes
preparation.reuse_claim: No reuse claim unless inputs and prepared buffers actually reused; full-call source remains the main comparison.

memory.execution_order: smoke first; remaining shapes in ascending estimated live bytes, largest anchor last
memory.preflight: Estimate and record bytes for original inputs, padded inputs, FP32 output, one result, and reference samples. Conservative estimate is not measured peak memory.
memory.on_preflight_over_budget: Record skipped_memory_preflight with estimate and limit; do not silently remove shape.
memory.on_device_oom: Record oom, clear executable/input buffers before the next case; retry only in a new immutable run.

correctness.input_reference: Use the exact BF16-quantized operands cast to NumPy float32, not the pre-quantization random source.
correctness.sampling: seeded without replacement, always including first and last row/column; record indices; reference uses all K
correctness.failure_policy: Record failures and measurements; failing rows cannot count as valid speedup wins. Fixed thresholds never change to rescue an arm.
correctness.scope: Finite synthetic numerical eligibility only; no bound on model quality or worst-case error.

smoke.purpose: Compile/shape/padding/numerical checks and cost calibration before broad campaign.

N1.purpose: Untuned implementations across 44 shapes; cubic_full is practical control, cubic_quadrant isolates split-form overhead.

N2.purpose: Matched tile effect and feasibility; these screen winners are provisional, not independently confirmed N5 claims.
N2.candidate_order: seeded balanced order; identical candidate list and attempts for every algorithm

N3.purpose: Two single-change ablations and their interaction, held at fixed tiles and precision.
N3.fallback_policy: No adaptive tile substitution; compile failure is a recorded result. A revised common tile requires a new protocol version.

N4.purpose: Numerical characterization across fixed inputs; accuracy failures and nonfinite values retained.

real_weights.policy: Optional future cohort only after recording checkpoint revision, tensor names, dtype, file hashes and activation provenance; never label these synthetic arrays as real weights.

execution_contract.commit_policy: Root orchestrator commits source snapshot before execution and records a commit after every completed or failed execution. Existing source snapshots and result directories are never overwritten.
execution_contract.resume: A retry/new version receives a new run id and references previous run ids; never appends measurements to a sealed run.
execution_contract.external_changes: Any device or environment change creates a new cohort; do not pool it silently with the original allocation.

deferred: Two-level Strassen: optional future experiment only, excluded from N1-N4.
N5 independent final tuning and fresh confirmation.
N6 profiling and N6a frozen selection-rule development.
v6e replication only after explicit later campaign activation.
Fused activations, residuals and end-to-end LLM quality are later N8-N9 work.
